$comment: Twelve entries across ten events. Budget is 12 for the whole plugin; a thirteenth requires deleting one.
PROTOCOL, because these are the cheap ways to ship a gate that enforces nothing:
- Exit 2 blocks. Exit 1 is a NON-blocking error and the tool RUNS.
- The event arrives on STDIN as JSON. TOOL_NAME / TOOL_INPUT env vars do not exist.
- type 'http' fails OPEN on non-2xx, timeout and connection error. Never use it for a gate.
- Quote ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}. The command goes to sh, and an install path holding a space
split it in two: every gate exited 127, which blocks nothing and says nothing.
Verify with `plugin/bin/claude-bp-doctor`, which proves each gate by attempting a
known-bad action rather than reading this file back.
`modules` is the hooks module, which runs inside Claude Code and is no hook entry: it
changes what the model reads of a long result, where WebSearch goes and what a listing of
agents says (decisions 0048, 0049, 0050). Where mods are off it is not loaded, and every
entry below works as before.
`fork` is a source like any other, and leaving it out of this matcher is not a
conservative default — it is this gate not running at all on a forked session.
`--fork-session` resumes a session under a NEW id in the SAME worktree, so the
fork gets no board, no registration, no reap and no pre-push arming, which is
the entire coordination layer, on exactly the workflow this product is for.
Enforcement is unaffected either way: `evidence-gate` adopts a missing record
at `branch_point`, never at HEAD, so an unregistered session is over-reported
rather than let through. What a fork loses is awareness, not the gate.
The only event that carries a pull request's NUMBER. PreToolUse records the
obligation and never sees the response, so every record used to say 0 and the
merge gate could not tell its own pull request from somebody else's (#135).
`update_pull_request` because closing one without merging is `state: closed` on
it, and nothing else sees that call: `gh pr close` is read by pre-tool instead.
`merge_pull_request` because only this event says the merge RAN. pre-tool judges
it and holds it; spent and settled there, a merge that then failed had taken the
founder's word and closed its cards (#232, #243, #268).
`enable_pr_auto_merge` for the same reason: it is `gh pr merge --auto` as a tool.
`gh pr create` prints the number, and only this event sees it. Left out while
catching it meant a process on every shell call, because an unlearned number
only meant 'do not judge'. A `+merge` that names the chat's open pull requests
made it a refusal instead: `gh pr merge 48` could not be matched to the pull
request the word covered, and was refused four times over (#241).
`gh pr merge` for the same reason the tool's merge is above: only this event
says it ran.
`if` (Claude Code 2.1.85, compound commands from 2.1.89) spawns the process only
for a shell line that runs `gh pr`; `if` holds one rule, so not one per verb.
Where it is not honoured the hook runs on every shell call, and it exits before
touching git.
After the turn, so the founder can write while the suite runs: a client that takes
no message while a hook holds the turn kept them out of the session for all of it,
and the run their message would have stopped (#277) never heard one. A refusal or
a question wakes the session (exit 2); a message from the founder, or the session
at work again, stops the run. An hour, because nobody waits on it now.
A `claude -p` whose process ends with its turn stops this hook with it: its finish
is judged where it lands instead, since a merge needs a green run (decision 0046).
